recipe.fingerprint: sha256: for each PRESENT metadata file in that order, name then raw bytes; then json.dumps((name, st_size, st_mtime_ns)).encode() per shard in sorted(set(weight_map.values())) order; then json.dumps(header_sha256_list).encode(), where each entry is the sha256 of a shard's raw header bytes (8 .. 8 + length) in the same sorted shard order
recipe.header_scope: the header declares names, dtypes, shapes and offsets; its digest is not a digest of tensor values
recipe.schema: pinned config (24 keys including cohere2_moe topology, tie_word_embeddings null, rms_norm_eps 1e-06, layer_norm_eps 1e-05), layer_types [full every 4th of 49], architectures [Cohere2MoeForCausalLM]; quantization or quantization_config object with per-module overrides (group_size int, bits 4 or 8) determining U32 weight and BF16 scales/biases shapes; 1226 tensors for the default 49-layer artifact; index keys exactly the header tensors; no lm_head, no mtp./eagle/draft names

modifications: FAMILIES gains 'north' (adapter mlx2.adapters.north_mini_code.NorthMiniCodeAdapter, the six-file metadata order, headers=True). Its required files are the ordinary route's sources: north_mini_code.py, external_draft_policy.py (adapter base class), runtime/models/cohere2_moe.py and switch_layers.py (model body and MoE layers), runtime/ubc_evict.py (shard loader) and runtime/tokenizer_integrity.py (tokenizer repair); the loaded-module closure check still binds every other loaded mlx2 module

artifact_family returns 'north' only for a config that passes the inspector's own pinned checks (north_config_refusal: the 24-key expected dict compared with !=, layer_types, architectures); any other cohere2_moe config (including incomplete ones) still refuses before any shard is touched

north_artifact_manifest (stdlib only): strict JSON (duplicate keys refused) for config, index and each header; weight_map a nonempty object of string shard names; speculative markers and an untied head refused; shard names non-empty, relative, without '..', resolving inside the artifact to an existing .safetensors file, and no two names for one file (resolved path or device/inode); full expected schema from config and quantization overrides (group_size <= 0 refused explicitly where the inspector would divide by zero); per shard: dtype in {BF16, U32}, int shapes >= 0, two int offsets within the payload, byte size = elements x dtype size, index entry naming this shard, no duplicate tensor across shards, no overlapping ranges; index tensor set equals header tensor set; observed == expected schema with bounded missing/extra/wrong counts

bounded reads (seams _open_fd, _read_fd, _fstat_fd): each shard is stat'ed, opened O_NOFOLLOW, and only its 8-byte little-endian length and then exactly that many header bytes are requested, with 0 < length <= min(64 MiB, size - 8); the path stat before open, the descriptor at open and after the read, and the path stat after the read must be the same file (device, inode, size, mtime_ns). Short reads, truncation and invalid lengths refuse explicitly

guarded metadata reads (root finding seq 3016): every North metadata file and the initial config.json of EVERY family (it is read before dispatch) must be a regular file itself (symlink refused), with st_nlink 1 and at most 256 MiB, refused before any byte is read; read through one O_NOFOLLOW descriptor to the stat size with the same four-field identity checked at open, after the read and at the path afterwards. A metadata name therefore cannot redirect a read into shard payload. Config parsing RecursionError becomes an explicit 'nests too deeply' refusal (root finding seq 3018); header and index nesting likewise

TOCTOU: the whole North collection (metadata hashes, shard stats, shard device/inode, header hashes, schema size) is taken twice and must be equal, so a change, or an identical-bytes replacement under a new inode, between the two refuses. KeyError/OverflowError/TypeError from collection become ValueError refusals; preflight and the post-run manifest already turn ValueError/OSError into refusals

adapter identity: adapter_identity_snapshot adds header_sha256 only when the adapter's identity carries it (Muse/Qwen snapshots unchanged); adapter_identity_refusals compares header_sha256 when the manifest has it; post_run_identity also compares header_sha256 and shard_file_ids. The constructed adapter's fingerprint, path, shard records and header digests must equal the preflight before any arm, and the snapshot is compared again after the arms
